items.title: Actual smooth gradient-arc exponential moment

source.anchor: Appendix D.1 Claim 1 proof and Claim 2, smooth s=1 moment; consumed by SPHMC Appendix A.4(2)
source.attribution: ASTIS source-proof-supported mathematical restatement and exposition, preserving the factor2 used in the proof and subsequent Claim 2. This is a dependency of Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang, Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. It is not the differing printed logarithmic Claim 1 formula or an author-endorsed repair.

items.statement: The vector gradient f(x) is the actual gradient of f at every x. For each displayed real r, F_r is measurable and integrable under the actual input law mu, its integral is at most 2 exp(10 d eta^2 lambda^2 beta^2), and the logarithm of its integral is at most log 2+10 d eta^2 lambda^2 beta^2.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with its Borel measurable structure, and d=finrank(E). Zero dimension is allowed. The real-valued function f is differentiable everywhere and its actual gradient is beta-Lipschitz, where beta>=0.
eta>0, lambda>=0, 12 beta^2 eta^2 lambda^2<=1, and h,x_plus in E satisfy norm(h-x_plus)<=sqrt(d eta).
The actual independent input law is mu=N(h,eta I) product N(0,eta I), explicitly the product of the pushforwards of standard Gaussian by z->h+sqrt(eta)z and z->sqrt(eta)z.
For each real r set theta=pi*r/2, gamma_r(x,z)=h+sin(theta)(x-h)+cos(theta)z, v_r(x,z)=(pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h)-sin(theta)z), W_r=<v_r,grad f(x_plus)-grad f(gamma_r)> and F_r=exp(lambda abs(W_r)).

bindings.boundary: This is the smooth s=1 source-proof-supported estimator moment, preserving the factor2 used by Claim 2. It is not a silent repair or proof of printed Claim 1 without log2. beta=0, d=0 and all real r are disclosed extensions. The actual center construction h=x0-eta grad f(x_plus), clipping, target log-weight mean identification, normalized Renyi error, initialization and terminal query cost remain separate. No full SPHMC or PBPS main result is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Smooth case s=1 in positive Euclidean dimension with beta>0.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite-dimensional real inner product space, including dimension zero, and beta>=0.
assumption_deltas.reason: The basis-independent argument and empty Gaussian product remain valid; beta=0 makes the true gradient constant. No division by beta is used.
The actual joint Gaussian arc law holds at every real angle.

assumption_deltas.source: h=x0-eta grad f(x_plus) with norm(h-x_plus)<=sqrt(d eta).
assumption_deltas.lean: Arbitrary h,x_plus subject to the same norm bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: The moment proof only uses this bound. Constructing the actual source center remains a later consumer.

assumption_deltas.source: Smooth differentiable potential with beta-Lipschitz gradient, eta>0, lambda>=0 and the smooth moment range.
assumption_deltas.lean: Differentiable real f, LipschitzWith beta on its actual gradient, eta>0, lambda>=0 and 12 beta^2 eta^2 lambda^2<=1.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source smooth range is expressed without division, so the valid zero-beta extension is visible.

assumption_deltas.source: The Claim 1 proof and Claim 2 use a factor2 exponential moment; printed Claim 1 logarithmic formula lacks log2.
assumption_deltas.lean: Integral exp(lambda abs(W))<=2 exp(10 d eta^2 lambda^2 beta^2), with log2 retained in the logarithmic form.
assumption_deltas.reason: The attributed source is the proof-supported factor2 contract, not the differing printed log statement. That separate possible-source-error is preserved and no repair is silently adopted.

assumption_deltas.source: Expectations of the actual Gaussian arc gradient estimator.
assumption_deltas.lean: Actual product of affine standard-Gaussian pushforwards; measurability and integrability are conclusions, and HasGradientAt identifies the gradient.
assumption_deltas.reason: These analytic obligations justify the source integration and log steps; they are proved rather than added as moment assumptions.
